referents.why: The possessive 'his' sits in 'his mother' in the second line, which is about the foolish son; w7 is the masculine singular foolish son, and the mother is his. The wise son of the first line is not the owner of this mother.

links.why: Plain waw joining two opposed proverb lines. The sense is contrast ('but' in the English), not cause, result or purpose, and the contrast type takes only explicit but-words, so the 'and' link stands.

none_fit.what: antithetic pair of lines joined by a plain waw; the contrast link needs an explicit but-word, and no group kind holds an antithetic pair
Antithetic couplet: the second line opposes the first, carried only by a plain waw. No link type covers antithesis without an explicit but-word.
Contrast marked only by a bare waw (Hebrew vav, English 'but'). The contrast link is for the word 'but' (אוּלָם, אֶפֶס כִּי) only, so this antithesis has no link type.

cant_tell.what: how far the writing group extends beyond this verse
cant_tell.why: The heading governs the collection that follows; this verse alone does not show where its part ends.

cant_tell.what: Whether the couplet is a parallel group
cant_tell.why: The second line restates roles with its verb elided, but its subject is a different son (wise, then foolish), so the parallel kind's condition of one shared subject does not hold. Not added.

cant_tell.what: A writing group for the heading cl0 ('the proverbs of Solomon')
cant_tell.why: The heading opens a collection that runs beyond this verse. A writing group needs its part from later verses, so it is held rather than built from this verse alone.
